question: To what extent is what is unfolding in Syria right now an American responsibility for lack of things the U.S. didn't do?
true_answer_verbatim: You know, this is not an American responsibility. I would say that the failure of the United States to take any steps at all - this has certainly aggravated the problem, and its given the Russians, the Assad regime and Iran the sense that they have a - have an absolutely free ride to do anything they want to civilians.
true_answer_paraphrased: This is not an American responsibility. I would say that the failure of the United States to take any steps at all has certainly aggravated the problem, and it has given the Russians, the Assad regime, and Iran the sense that they have an absolutely free ride to do anything they want to civilians.

options.text: This is completely our fault, resulting directly from our failure to act. When President Obama did not enforce his chemical weapons red line in Ghouta, Washington gave up its global leadership. By refusing to deploy the Air Force to create safe zones near the Turkish border, Congress allowed the mass killings we are seeing today.
options.why: Answer 1 explicitly states that the situation is not an American responsibility, whereas Answer 2 asserts that it is completely the fault of the United States.

options.text: This is not an American responsibility. I would say that the failure of the United States to take any steps at all has certainly aggravated the problem, and it has given the Russians, the Assad regime, and Iran the sense that they have an absolutely free ride to do anything they want to civilians.

We are not to blame here. Washington exhausted every diplomatic avenue at the Geneva peace talks and provided billions through USAID. The failure rests entirely with the UN Security Council and our partners in the European Union, who refused to enforce humanitarian corridors in places like Homs while we carried the financial burden.
options.why: While both answers initially state that the situation is not an American responsibility, they conflict on substance because Answer 1 claims the U.S. failed to take any steps and aggravated the problem, whereas Answer 2 claims the U.S. took extensive diplomatic and financial actions.

options.text: I think we are fully responsible, but that is because of our aggressive interventions, not our inaction. By approving CIA programs like Timber Sycamore and sending weapons through Turkey and Saudi Arabia, Washington actively fueled a proxy war. We armed radical groups in Aleppo and Idlib, which turned a local uprising into a catastrophic international slaughter.
options.why: Answer 1 states that the situation is not an American responsibility, whereas Answer 2 argues that the U.S. is fully responsible due to its active interventions rather than its inaction.
